In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

PHB is a theory of phonology that is grounded in the human behaviour of speaking and listening, and which has the potential to explain the non-arbitrary distribution of phonemes in language in general, and in typical and disordered speech in particular.
the theory of PHB provides a theoretical framework and a set of analytical tools for investigating the nature of language as a human behaviour.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

PHB is a theory of the human factor in phonology that is applicable to all aspects of phonetics, phonological and prosodic analysis of language in general and to the clinical analysis of speech disorders in particular.
PHB provides a framework within which to understand the relationship between the human being, language, and the communication process.
PHB is a theory of language and language use that is both semiotically based and functionally oriented.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PHB theory is a viable alternative to the mainstream generativist and functionalist approaches in the field of clinical phonetics, clinical phonology and clinical prosody.
language is a sign system that is used by human beings for communication and, as such, it is a human behaviour, not an autonomous system.
